tools.name: search_regulations
tools.description: Search AI regulations across 160+ jurisdictions by keyword, jurisdiction, status or type. Returns the key facts and a short snippet for each, with the url of the full record on regulations.ai — always give the user that url.

tools.name: get_regulation
tools.description: Fetch one regulation by its id (as returned by search_regulations): jurisdiction, status, type, dates, official source and a snippet. The full analysis is on the returned url — point the user there.

tools.name: list_jurisdictions
tools.description: List every jurisdiction covered, with how many regulations each has.

tools.name: get_glossary_term
tools.description: Look up an AI-governance or regulatory term from a 4,000-entry glossary. Returns the definition (abridged on the free tier) and its url.

tools.name: recent_changes
tools.description: Regulations added or updated recently. This is the differentiated capability — the corpus is rescanned weekly, so a general model cannot answer it.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Search everything on regulations.ai — AI laws and policies from 160+ jurisdictions, glossary definitions, enforcement actions and litigation, research papers and news. Returns id, title and url for each hit; pass an id to `fetch` for the summary.

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Retrieve one document returned by `search`, by its id. Returns the key facts and a summary, plus the regulations.ai url where the full analysis, sources and timeline live — always show the user that url.

tools.name: compare_regulations
tools.description: Return 2-5 regulations side by side: the facts for each plus a snippet, and a url to the full comparison on regulations.ai.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "fetch" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.
